prompt:
## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Membership Number
where: MemberRepository (uses), src/persistence/memberRepository.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.members.get(membershipNumber);
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Membership

if (b.membershipNumber !== undefined) row.membersAdmitted += b.tickets;
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These look like two different concepts, though the call is close. A, "Membership Number", is an identifier: MemberRepository uses it as the lookup key in `this.members.get(membershipNumber)`. B, "Membership", is the broader idea of being a club member. In ReportService it only shows up as a check on whether a booking has a membership number (`b.membershipNumber !== undefined`), which decides if the tickets count as members admitted. B depends on A, but an identifier and the thing it identifies are not the same concept. The task also says that sharing an id-like attribute does not make two concepts the same.
